historical_claims.anchor: A sequence of probability laws converges weakly to another law when the expected value of every bounded continuous test function under the sequence converges to its expected value under the limiting law.
This is weak convergence: the probability laws of the standardized errors approach a normal law.
That is a route to almost-sure weak convergence of the empirical distribution toward the population distribution for independent identically distributed real-valued observations.
historical_claims.source_locator: Empirical distribution law via strong law

description: Distinguishes convergence in distribution from convergence of individual outcomes, explaining why weak convergence does not automatically control unbounded expectations.
